title: Note text: the edited Note keeps its Draft text until Editing ends
lede: Before this PR, #41 kept the **Draft text** in the ui store, so each keystroke still called `ui.typed` and notified every ui store subscriber. Now the textarea of the Note in **Editing** (`NoteEditor`) keeps the Draft text in its own React state, and **typing touches no store**. When the editor mounts, it lends the ui store a way to read that text (`holdDraft`). However Editing ends, the Notes store reads it at once and saves it to the Note, before the action that ended Editing carries on. Delete-then-Undo and `pagehide` therefore still get the typed text.

files.question: Where does the Draft text live while typing?
files.summary: `NoteEditor` keeps it in `useState`, mirrored in a ref, and lends a reader to the ui store in a layout effect.
files.owns: The Draft text itself, from mount (the Note's saved `text`) until it unmounts.
files.never: Writes to a store while typing, or saves the text itself.
files.tested: `src/editing.browser.test.tsx`, `Draft text`: counts updates of both stores while typing; every ending; × delete then Undo; Profiler.

files.question: How does the Notes store reach text held inside a component?
files.summary: `holdDraft(id, read)` keeps the reader in a closure variable outside the store's state and returns a release; `readDraft(id)` calls it.
files.owns: At most one lent reader, for the Note in Editing only.
files.never: Notifies anyone when a reader is lent or released: it isn't state.
files.tested: `src/notes/notesActions.test.ts`: `an editor that has unmounted lends nothing, unless another has lent since`, `a Draft text lent for a Note not in Editing is ignored`.

files.question: Which transition ended Editing?
files.summary: `draftText`, `typed` and `endedDraft` are gone; `endedEditing(before, after)` names the Note whose Editing ended.
files.owns: The rule for how Editing ends, through the single exit `end`.
files.tested: `src/ui/uiStore.test.ts`, unchanged; and through the Notes store tests.

files.question: Who saves the Draft text, and when?
files.summary: Its ui store subscriber: when `endedEditing` names a Note, it reads that Note's Draft text and calls `setText`, synchronously inside the `set` that ended Editing.
files.owns: Saving the Draft text to the Note, and reading the Undo snapshot only after it.
files.never: Runs on a keystroke: typing doesn't change the ui store at all now.
files.tested: `src/notes/notesActions.test.ts`, `Draft text`: every ending, `pageHidden`, delete then Undo, nothing typed.

files.question: Is the text saved when the tab closes?
files.summary: Unchanged: `pageHidden()` ends Editing, which saves the Draft text, and only then `saving.flush()` writes the Local copy.
files.owns: The order of the two calls on `pagehide`.
files.tested: Only the store side (`pageHidden` saves the Draft text); the listener's order isn't covered, see notes.

files.question: How is it proved in a real browser?
files.summary: The `Draft text` tests type with real keys and count updates of both stores; a new ending, the × on another Note, joins the list.
files.owns: The user-visible behaviour: every ending keeps the text, delete then Undo, no other Note re-renders.
files.never: Calls store actions to type: it goes through the real textarea.
files.tested: Is the test. `typing updates no store…` failed before the change with `ui: 4`.

files.question: How are the store rules tested without React?
files.summary: A stand-in editor keeps its text in a plain object and lends it through `holdDraft`, as `NoteEditor` does.
files.owns: Every ending, `pageHidden`, delete then Undo, nothing typed, and the reader's release and Editing check.

scenarios.name: Note A is in Editing; type `big `, then press Escape

steps.title: The editor mounts and lends its reader
steps.explain: When A enters Editing, `NoteEditor` mounts with `draftText` set to A's saved text. Its layout effect runs before paint, so an Editing that ends in the very next event still finds the reader. `holdDraft` returns its release, which React calls on unmount. The reader reads the ref, not the state, because it is called from outside React, after the last render.

steps.title: Each keystroke
steps.explain: `onChange` updates the ref and the component's own state, and nothing else. Only `NoteEditor` re-renders. The browser test subscribes to both stores and counts `{ notes: 0, ui: 0 }` after typing; before this PR it counted 4 ui updates for 4 keys.

steps.title: keydown Escape: Editing ends through the single exit
steps.explain: The textarea reports Escape; `end` clears `editingId`. Zustand calls subscribers synchronously inside this `set`, so what follows runs before `escaped()` returns.

run.from: function end(state: EditingState, reason: EditingEnd): EditingState {
run.to: return state.editingId === null ? state : { ...NOT_EDITING, editingEndedBy: reason };

steps.title: The Notes store saves the Draft text, once
steps.explain: `endedEditing` sees A's id before and none after, so the subscriber reads A's Draft text through the lent reader and saves it. React hasn't re-rendered yet, so the editor is still mounted; even so, the reader only reads a ref. That is one Notes store update, which the Local copy saves 300 ms later.

steps.title: React re-renders: the editor unmounts and takes its reader back
steps.explain: The release clears the reader only if it is still this editor's. When Editing moves to another Note, the old editor's cleanup and the new editor's `holdDraft` run in the same commit, in an order this code doesn't rely on. If the old editor cleared unconditionally, it could wipe the new editor's reader.

run.from: // Only its own: by now another editor may have lent one.

scenarios.name: Type in Note A, then delete A with its ×, then Undo

steps.title: deleteNote reports the delete before reading the Undo snapshot
steps.explain: `deleted(id)` ends Editing on A, so the subscriber saves the Draft text into A first. Only then is A read for Undo, so the snapshot has the typed text. In the other order, Undo would bring back A's text from before Editing.

steps.title: End Editing, then flush
steps.explain: `pageHidden()` ends Editing; the subscriber saves the Draft text and schedules a Local copy write, which `flush` then writes at once. This file didn't change. The text now comes from the editor's reader instead of the ui store, but it is read at the same moment.

scenarios.name: Nothing typed: Escape changes no Note

steps.title: The saved text comes back unchanged
steps.explain: The reader returns the text the editor started from, so `setText` finds it equal and returns the same state: Zustand notifies nobody and the Local copy isn't written. Before this PR, `draftText` stayed `null` instead; the outcome is the same.

notes.title: Why a lent reader, not an unmount effect
notes.detail: Saving in the editor's unmount cleanup would be simpler, but it runs after React re-renders, which is too late: `deleteNote` reads its Undo snapshot, and `pagehide` flushes, in the same call that ended Editing. The counter-argument: the ui store now holds a function that isn't state. It sits outside the state on purpose, so lending one notifies nobody.

notes.title: Where the Editing rule is checked
notes.detail: `holdDraft` ignores a Note that isn't in Editing. That check sits in `uiStore.ts`, not in the pure transitions of `editing.ts`, because the reader isn't state. The code review flagged it as a judgement call; it was left as it is.

notes.title: A remount would drop typed text
notes.detail: If `NoteEditor` remounted mid-Editing, `useState(text)` would start again from the saved text. No path does that today: Notes are keyed by id, and the editor's effect depends only on `id` and `ui`. Under #41 the text lived in the store and would have survived.

notes.title: Tests that check less than the issue's wording
notes.detail: The Profiler wraps the whole Note, so it can't tell A's textarea re-rendering from all of A re-rendering; it shows no other Note re-renders. The `pagehide` order in `main.tsx` is still not covered by a test.
